entries.title: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds
entries.summary: Dream-RSI turns an agent's accumulated discovery trees into exact replay simulators for the explored search space, uses them to cheaply evaluate and rewrite exploration policies, then redeploys the improved policy so each live round expands the worlds available for the next round.

entries.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
entries.summary: ScienceBuddy couples two improvement loops: an inner loop evolves the scientific-agent harness while holding the model fixed, and an outer loop trains the model under the improved harness, turning researcher requests, feedback, and execution evidence into continual-learning tasks and rubrics.

entries.title: Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations
entries.summary: ICML replaces static agent memory heuristics with co-evolving Planner and Trigger policies trained online from delayed conversational rewards, so storage and retrieval decisions improve from accumulated interaction feedback rather than remaining fixed after deployment.

entries.title: Right Direction, Wrong Step: Geometric Analysis of Finite-Step Failure in Looped Transformers
entries.summary: This analysis isolates a concrete failure mode in looped Transformers: an iteration can point in a locally useful direction yet move too far. Curvature-aware analysis and fractional readout steps recover positive reference-utility gains on many otherwise harmful loop updates, suggesting step-size control as a route to safer test-time depth scaling.

entries.title: LSTM-UT and Recurrent-Depth Transformers on Cellular Automata
entries.summary: LSTM-UT adds bounded gated memory to recurrent-depth Transformer computation and outperforms both a state-only Block Universal Transformer and cache-growing CoTFormer on depth extrapolation and delayed recall, highlighting memory design as a key inductive bias for repeated computation.

entries.title: MoRE: Mixture of Reused Experts
entries.summary: MoRE hybridizes recurrent-style parameter reuse with mixture-of-experts capacity by sharing expert pools across adjacent depth layers while keeping layer-specific routers and depth embeddings; it improves perplexity and downstream quality over standard MoEs and weight-sharing baselines at matched parameter and compute budgets.

entries.title: Infinite-Parameter LLMs: Generating and Adapting Weights from Live Data
entries.summary: Infinite-Parameter LLMs propose a hypernetwork that compiles live interaction data into low-rank feed-forward weight modulations, while an online Bayesian latent belief updates those generated weights across a session. The architecture aims to persist new knowledge in fixed-footprint adaptive weights instead of repeatedly carrying it in the prompt.

entries.title: ThinkFlow: Self-Evolving Probabilistic Latent Memory for Lifelong Conversational Agents
entries.summary: ThinkFlow compresses conversational history into probabilistic latent memory skills and continuously refines them at test time with self-supervised next-user-utterance prediction, providing an end-to-end architecture for label-free lifelong personalization rather than static textual memory.

entries.title: Beyond Episodic AI: Cognitive Field Networks for Biologically Inspired Persistent Cognition
entries.summary: Cognitive Field Networks use a recurrent Transformer whose organized hidden field re-enters later inference, creating a history-dependent state that can persist and be renewed across cycles without an explicit episodic-memory operation; the experiments probe how learned recurrence supports persistent cognition beyond the trained horizon.

entries.title: Learning from Reliable Negatives: Confidence-Anchored Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Grounding
entries.summary: Confidence-Anchored Negative Learning adapts a GUI-grounding model at test time using coordinate-token confidence to identify reliable negative supervision, avoiding brittle positive pseudo-labels while substantially improving grounding accuracy on difficult ScreenSpot evaluations.

entries.title: Sparse MLLM Anchors, Dense Adaptation: Breaking the Self-Referential Loop in Wild Test-Time Adaptation
entries.summary: MASA improves online test-time adaptation by querying a frozen multimodal LLM for a sparse set of semantic anchors, propagating those descriptions through an online prototype memory, and using the resulting external semantic target to adapt lightweight model parameters instead of relying only on the model's own potentially erroneous predictions.

entries.title: Bridging the Confidence Gap: Temperature Scaling for Calibrating Test-Time Prompt Tuning
entries.summary: CoTS targets a weakness of test-time prompt tuning: adaptation can improve accuracy while damaging calibration. It temperature-scales adapted predictions toward the confidence profile of the zero-shot model and combines this with weak-strong augmentation ensembling, improving calibration without giving back the adaptation gains.
